acquisition method: The mass spectrometer was operated in a data-dependent mode.
alkylation reagent: Free cysteines were alkylated by adding iodoacetamide at a final concentration of 8.3 mM to the samples for a 1 h incubation under agitation at room temperature in the dark.
alkylation concentration: Free cysteines were alkylated by adding iodoacetamide at a final concentration of 8.3 mM to the samples for a 1 h incubation under agitation at room temperature in the dark.
cleavage agent: Samples were pre-digested with 1.6 μg of Lys-C (Pierce) and incubated at 37 °C for 2 h under agitation and digested with bead-immobilized trypsin (40 μL of beads per 250 μg of protein; Pierce) for 16 h at 37 °C under agitation.
collision energy: The full MS scan was followed by MS/MS for the top 10 precursor ions in each cycle with a normal collision energy of 28 and dynamic exclusion of 30 s.
enrichment method: tissue sections were resuspended in the cytosolic (“C”) buffer of the CNMCS compartmental protein extraction kit (Millipore) and disrupted by vortexing.
fractionation method: Equivalent peptide amounts were fractionated via high-pH reversed-phase HPLC.
instrument: before nanoelectrospray using a QExactive mass spectrometer (Thermo).
ionization type: before nanoelectrospray using a QExactive mass spectrometer (Thermo).
labeling: For each protein, total precursor ion intensity (further referred to as “peptide intensity”) was calculated as the sum of MS1-precursor-ion-peak areas for all identified peptides of the given protein.
reduction reagent: Disulfide bonds were reduced by adding 5 mM dithiothreitol to the samples for a 1 h incubation under agitation at room temperature.
reduction concentration: Disulfide bonds were reduced by adding 5 mM dithiothreitol to the samples for a 1 h incubation under agitation at room temperature.
